name: Vardenafil North American Pivotal Trial
question: Does as-needed vardenafil improve erectile function compared with placebo in men with erectile dysfunction?

design.population: 805 men aged at least 18 years with erectile dysfunction for more than 6 months and at least 50% failure of erection maintenance on four baseline intercourse attempts at 54 US and Canadian centers.
design.description: Multicenter, double-blind, fixed-dose randomized superiority trial
design.locator: Journal pp763-765, Study Design, Inclusion Criteria, Patient Population

verdictNote: All three doses met the adjusted significance threshold on three coprimary measures at week 12.
takeaway: In a North American randomized trial, as-needed vardenafil 5, 10, or 20 mg improved week-12 erectile-function scores, penetration, and intercourse completion versus placebo; all three doses met the prespecified multiplicity-adjusted threshold.

reports.label: Primary efficacy and safety report
reports.citation: Hellstrom WJG, Gittelman M, Karlin G, et al. "Vardenafil for Treatment of Men With Erectile Dysfunction: Efficacy and Safety in a Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Trial." *J Androl.* 2002;23(6):763-771. doi:10.1002/j.1939-4640.2002.tb02332.x
reports.followUp: 12-week prespecified primary assessment; treatment continued to 26 weeks
reports.followUpLocator: Journal pp764-765, Efficacy Variables; p767, Figures 2-3

results.measure: Week-12 mean score, 1-30 scale; last observation carried forward
results.note: Baseline means: 12.5, 13.4, 12.8, and 13.6, respectively; prespecified Bonferroni threshold P<0.0167.
